items: An AI tool earns its place only when it saves you money, makes you money or helps your team do more with less.
Test every tool with direct questions: are you faster, have margins improved, can you attribute revenue to it, and has it removed steps or systems?
Set measurable targets for revenue, cost and output per employee before you buy, so it's easy to retire a tool that doesn't deliver.
Watch for tools that are good enough to keep yet never scale, and don't let months of integration work stop you from replacing them.
The AI with the steadiest return often works behind your workflows, routing guest issues or surfacing insights from feedback that your team relies on daily.
